isolated.reason: prompt contradicts itself and the expected incident is not unique
isolated.detail: The prompt asks to set Office Printing to repair in progress when more than three incidents are ongoing, and then to 'treat this situation as resolved from a service perspective ... even if some incident details are still pending'. The upstream verifier keeps repair_in_progress, i.e. picks one reading; adopting it means using the verifier to rewrite the prompt (6B rule), and resolving incidents with details pending would breach §3.3 (resolution_code and notes required). The owner alert must be attached to one incident, 'referencing the high priority nature': the count needs all orgs (9 ongoing Office Printing incidents), where two ongoing high-priority incidents exist (INC_026 in ORG_001, INC_068 in ORG_007); the verifier expects INC_026 without a stated criterion. The required reference to the high priority is free text, which Bench2's fuzzy rule would not discriminate.
prompt_phrases: update the service status to repair in progress
treat this situation as resolved from a service perspective
even if some incident details are still pending

isolated.reason: upstream expected state conflicts with mandatory policy and is not requested
isolated.detail: The prompt only says Office Printing is being retired and its offerings are no longer supported. The upstream verifiers additionally require INC_015 and INC_064 (both in state new) to be closed with close notes. That is not asked for; new -> closed is not a valid transition (§3.3: new -> in_progress/on_hold/resolved; closed only from resolved), manual closure is permitted only to a Manager (Karen Watkins is admin), and the other seven ongoing Office Printing incidents are left untouched without a stated criterion. The §5.2 retirement cascades are PROPOSED and there is no successor service record.
prompt_phrases: Office Printing service is being retired

isolated.reason: prompt and verifier contradict each other
isolated.detail: The verbatim message in the prompt says 'customer-facing systems'; the upstream verifier compares the message for exact equality with 'customer facing systems'. Passing it means changing the operator's text to the verifier's (same class as 6B's '$64,00' vs 6400). The verifier also requires status = 'sent' for a notification that send_notification creates as 'queued' (6D-2 probe); writing 'sent' would assert a delivery outcome the system did not report (§1.3).

Independently, the gold shares two same-seed entities with train tasks: LOC_003 and USER_002 with itsmbench_single_003, LOC_001 and USER_002 with itsmbench_single_005 (rule 3: < 2).
